messages.subject: Hierarchical Multivariate Normal Models for Quantile Estimation: Inference Problems!
parts:
Hi folks,

I'm working with hierarchical multivariate normal models and having trouble getting them to recover the parameters from test data. This might be because I'm unwittingly simulating weird test data, or because I'm dealing with too little data, or a weak identification problem, or maybe I am just poorly parameterising the model so the sampler is ill-conditioned. The R and stan files are attached here. 

I'm simulating a 10-dimensional multivariate normal variable which realises across 5 different sites, once in each site. I am mimicking the situation in which I have estimates of 10 empirical quantiles and their standard errors from 5 different data sets of the same outcome. I have the realisations and their standard errors, so using the result in Koenker & Basset 1978 I can therefore construct the entire variance-covariance matrix of sampling error in each site. I want to estimate the hyperparameters: the grand mean vector, and the variance-covariance matrix that governs the variability of the realisations of empirical quantiles across sites. 

I tried 2 models in stan: (1) allow a fully general hyper-variance-covariance structure with LKJ priors (on cholesky factors, of course), and (2) parameterise the covariance matrix by a scale vector and a correlation matrix that has an AR(1) structure, so it only has 11 unknown parameters, the 10 scales and the 1 "rho" from the AR(1). Both of them work very poorly even when the model in (2) is correct about the matrix structure.... actually method (1) works better even in that case.

Stan warning messages from my models have encouraged me to push up adapt_delta to 0.9 and max_treedepth to 12, but the resulting sampler still seems to get divergent pairs. Right now, running the files as attached, I get things like this for both models:

Warning messages:
1: There were 2747 divergent transitions after warmup. Increasing adapt_delta above 0.9 may help. 
2: There were 1 transitions after warmup that exceeded the maximum treedepth. Increase max_treedepth above 12. 
3: Examine the pairs() plot to diagnose sampling problems

Sorry to bother you with what may well be just me making a silly mistake or making demands on the data that it can't meet, but I really thought that method (2) would not be too demanding! so maybe there's some pathology in how I'm setting up the model or data or etc. 

I appreciate any and all thoughts, suggestions, or feedback.  Thank you all so much for your time. 

Cheers
Rachael

parts:
I didn't understand your matrix construction in either transformed
data or transformed parameters --- maybe someone else will be more
familiar.

I wouldn't define sigma_sq and then take square roots --- go the
other way around and just model sigma.

Are you getting excptions that Sigma isn't positive definite?

Also, you want to stay with Cholesky factors through the whole
process; it's way more efficient.

There are other efficiency gains to be had here, but let's get
the model working first.

How are you measuring reconstruction? Are your posteriors not
calibrated in the sense that roughly 50% of the parameters don't fall in
their posterior 50% intervals? You won't get exact reconstruction of parameters
except in the limit of increasing data sizes.

The prior on rho expects strong positive correlation throughout (2.5 standard
deviations just to get to correlation = 0).

You probably aren't going to be able to fit a multilevel model with
a fresh covariance matrix for each observation:

for(k in 1:K){
y[k] ~ multi_normal(beta_0_k[k], Sigma_y_k[k]);

The problem is that you only have a single observation y[k] with which to fit
an entire covariance matrix Sigma_y_k[k].

- Bob

Don't despair --- that just means there's probably a bug in the code.

I would strongly recommend starting with simpler models and building
up, so when you get to the thing that breaks, it's easier to diagnose.

The mantra is: design top down, build and debug bottom up.

I'm trying to basically create a multivariate version of the 8 schools model from Rubin (1981), but the vectors have to be ordered because I am trying to fit a set of empirical quantiles.
Are you simulating data to fit from the correct model with fixed Sigma_y_k?

> I have the observed quantiles (a 10 dimensional vector called y[k] for site k) and the standard errors on the quantiles, which I can transform into the matrix Sigma_y_k[k] using a known formula (from Koenker & Basset 1978 / Mosteller 1942).

You just want to make sure you're fitting the model with
data simulated from the model. Otherwise, there's no guarantee
it'll fit when the model's misspecified.

parts:
Hi Bob (and anyone else reading this),

Sorry for the long radio silence! I'm back working on this problem now. I think we had hit on 2 issues: either there is a bug, or the way I simulated the data didn't actually have the dependence structure that I thought it had (or both). I have worked on the second issue for the moment, being unable to find a bug yet. 

Just to re-cap, I'm trying to model K vectors of estimated quantiles from a set of K continuous distributions. I have enough samples from each distribution that I know the estimated quantiles are approximately distributed as a multivariate normal, with a covariance matrix of known form (result from Mosteller 1946 and probably Laplace earlier than that). So within each site, the vector of quantiles has a MVN sampling distribution and I can estimate the relevant covariance matrix of that sampling distribution. Then I want to throw a hierarchical model on top, shrinking these vectors together across sites. 

I got the model to recover parameters of test data without the hierarchical part. Now I am having trouble with the hierarchy. The main issue seems to be estimating the parent covariance matrix (Sigma). As far as I can see, this is not something I can test on a simpler model than the one I use here, because without a hierarchical model that has K > 1, this Sigma does not exist / isn't identifiable. However, it should be identifiable from K > 1 draws from the hierarchical model (although it will be noisily estimated).

So I did 2 things: (1) I simulated data from the stan model itself, (2) I simulated data from a continuous univariate K-block hierarchical distribution directly, then estimated the K sets of quantiles, which are then fed into the hierarchical MVN model. 

(1) Didn't work at all (although I may have made a mistake). Exactly the same problem arises as before. And the model takes forever to sample. This makes me think I really must have a bug somewhere. The R file for this is the file name that ends in "from stan simulation fix SEs".

(2) Actually works great for K < 10 or so! I tried a few different variances out here and the model works great on all of them. But it did not work at all for large K: the diagonal elements of Sigma are not way too small, equal to the off diagonals (but the model inference is correct for the off diagonals). This kind of weirdness is confusing to me. Any idea what could be happening? The R file for this one is the file name that ends in "v2". 

I want to flag something here: The *true* dependency structure in the MVN model is not that clear, because the vectors are ordered. That ordering induces a mechanical positive correlation between draws because if quantile "t" is drawn higher than average, then quantile "t+1" must be more likely to be higher than average in order to be higher than "t". I find that this correlation grows stronger as I increase the variance (diagonal of Sigma) in my test runs, which makes intuitive sense to me since if we get a very extreme high draw of quantile t, it becomes almost certain that t+1 will have to be above average just to preserve the ordering. 

I definitely think at least part of the problem with my "simplified" covariance matrix estimation before is that I actually didn't account for this mechanical correlation from the ordered nature of the vector. However, seems like I still have some bug to iron out here as this does not explain the results completely, and the unconstrained covariance matrix is doing well for K < 10 and poorly otherwise. 

Any further advice on any angle of this very ugly knot of a problem is much appreciated. Sorry for returning to the thread on a friday afternoon! I won't abandon it again. 

Cheers
Rachael

But why do they give such different output? What is "ordered" doing exactly? And why does having a line like:

messages.subject: Re: Hierarchical Multivariate Normal Models for Quantile Estimation: Inference Problems!
parts:
ok! The interplay between ordered types and vector types is definitely one of the issues. if I change that final vector drawn in the hierarchy to be of type ordered, the code works as intended! 

I will make a new general thread about this interaction between ordered types and vector types since this seems like a stand-alone problem -- I will create a minimal reproducible example to illustrate just this issue alone. 

For my original problem here, I want to note that I also had made a dumb mistake before in simulating the data, which was to take in the mean output instead of a single draw -- I thought I was simulating a single draw from a single chain, in which case the mean IS the single draw, but I forgot that stan has a default chains = 4. Having fixed those 2 issues, the model works pretty well although it still seems to do something weird with the Sigma that I think is related to the ordering I've imposed on the vectors. 

Basically, if I say ordered_draw ~ multi_normal(ordered_mean, Sigma) for some known ordered_mean and Sigma, that Sigma does not map exactly to the true_Sigma from which the draw is being drawn because the ordering creates additional positive covariance between draws for the reasons I outlined in an earlier post. But moreover, I now realise that (holding all else equal) having a higher variance in slot Sigma[i,i] means that the covariance between Sigma[i,i+1] is pushed up too since when extreme draws realise in slot [i], extreme draws have to realise in slot [i+1] to keep the ordering. This seems like an inherent property of drawing an ordered vector object and not a problem. Happy to hear opinions to the contrary, however.
